# BSC (Bharat Steel Group) — Sales Call Knowledge Base (auto-distilled)

## Corpus summary
This corpus is a large concatenation of real call-center/field-sales recordings for BSC (Bharat Steel Group), a Chennai-based steel trading/stockist business. A genuine sales signal is present in a meaningful minority of calls — enquiries for **TMT rebar, structural steel (ISMB/ISMC/angles/channels/flats/SHS), MS plates & sheets (checkered and plain), CR coils, and round bars** — mixed heavily with **non-sales operational chatter** (MTC/tag/test-certificate follow-up, loading/crane/driver coordination, billing/payment-charge disputes, cutting-machine ("G2") operator instructions, and a large amount of personal/unrelated Hindi-Gujarati conversation under "Vishal" that has nothing to do with steel sales). Per the brief, all operational-only and non-sales calls were excluded from the analysis below; only calls with rate quotes, quantity/order discussion, stock checks, or objections were used.

Because genuine negotiation-heavy sales calls are a relatively small slice of the full corpus (most of the "sales" calls are short, transactional rate-check or stock-check exchanges), this KB stays close to what is actually evidenced rather than extrapolating a full playbook. Dominant customer types are **fabricators, small contractors/engineers, other traders/distributors, and earth-moving/structural companies** largely around Chennai, Tamil Nadu (with a few Mumbai/Jamshedpur/Vizag-origin enquiries).

## Products & brand ladder
Evidenced product lines:
- **TMT rebar** — grades FE 500 / 500D / 550D; sizes 8–32 mm. "550 500 தான் manufacture ஆகும்" [only 500/550 grade gets manufactured]. CRS (cold rolled/corrosion-resistant?) TMT also referenced, available only in 500D in some stock: "CRS-ல 500D தான் sir வரும்" [Only 500D comes in CRS].
- **Structural steel** — ISMB, ISMC (channel), angles (L-angle, equal/unequal), SHS/rectangular & square pipes, flats (e.g., "300x150" vs "300x140" I-beam/channel options with weight/flange trade-offs).
- **MS Plates & Sheets** — checkered plate, plain plate (2mm–25mm+), CR sheet (0.6mm, IS 513 spec mentioned), sizes like 4x8, 2500x6300mm standard coil-cut sizes.
- **Round bars / flats** for fabrication and bolt-thread rolling.
- Brands/sources mentioned: **SAIL (சைல்)**, **Vizag/RINL (விசாக், "Vaisakh")**, **Tata Steel**, **JSW**, and a generic "sale"/local brand distinction. Customers often ask specifically for brand+origin tag match (SAIL tag vs Vizag tag issue is a recurring dispute, see below). Grades like **E250, E350** also quoted for structural sections (E350 carries ~₹3,000 extra per the Vinayaga/V R Earth Movers-style calls).
- Company appears to primarily stock/sell **Vizag/RINL-origin material** currently, with occasional short supply of Tata/SAIL-grade variants, pushing customers to local/alternate brands when a specific mill is out of stock.

## Real rates & terms (only rates that actually appear in the calls)
- TMT: "₹12-32 வச்சுக்கோங்க ... ₹64" [for 12–32mm sizes keep ₹64, previously ₹68, ₹67] — Dindigul quote, transport-inclusive; "Chennai-ஆ இருந்தா இதுல இருந்து ₹1500 குறையும்" [₹1,500 less if delivery is Chennai].
- "65.500" per the V R Earth Movers 8mm sheet enquiry for 20 tons; later escalated to "65, 67, 68" range across calls as market moved.
- ISMB/structural: "300, 140 ₹60" vs "300, 150 ₹63" — same item, different section weight (42 vs 46 kg/m), ₹3,000/ton price gap explained by flange/weight difference.
- Plate rates fluctuating: "61 ₹ போயிட்டு இருக்கு" (plate), "62," "63," "64" across different weeks — clearly a volatile, near-daily-changing commodity rate.
- TMT size-based premium structure (VIMALADEVI/VJR/Zetwork calls): "16 to 25 — 65,000; 12mm — 67; 10mm — 68/69; 8mm — 70" (smaller diameter = higher ₹/ton due to lower demand/availability).
- E350 grade carries "₹3000 extra" vs E250 base.
- Standard commercial terms stated repeatedly: **"+ GST + loading + transport extra"** — basic/ex-works rate is quoted first, then additions.
- Minimum quantity/ready-stock constraints: cut-to-size sheets/coils often require "coil cut பண்ணி தான் கொடுக்கணும்" [must coil-cut before supply], causing 1-day-plus delay; full coil purchase sometimes offered as a workaround at better/flat rate.
- Credit vs advance payment pricing difference acknowledged: "Credit-ல போயிடுச்சு ... 1 month" leads to price being less favorable than advance payment — implicit evidence of **advance-payment discount / credit-markup**.
- Validity windows are short and explicitly communicated: "validity 2 days" is stated as a reason discounts can't be reopened.
- Loading is sometimes offered free as a concession instead of cutting the per-ton rate ("loading free பண்ணலாம்").

## Objection Playbook
1. **"Rate too high / competitor cheaper"** (very common)
 - Customer: "வேற ஒரு ₹60 rate கொஞ்சம் குறைக்க கூடாதா?" [Can't you reduce to ₹60?]
 - Rep response pattern: hold firm on rate, cite market increase, and defend validity: "loading charges கூட கம்மி பண்ண முடியாது sir ... rate எல்லாமே increase ஆயிடுச்சு."
 - Escalation tactic from customer: invoking long relationship/loyalty and MD-level past exceptions ("MD கிட்டயே request பண்ணி கேட்டு..."). Reps should acknowledge loyalty but separate it from current cost-based pricing; avoid reopening unrelated fee lines (loading/payment charges) as a bargaining chip mid-dispute — one call shows this confusing both sides and prolonging the call unnecessarily.

2. **"Brand/tag mismatch" (SAIL vs Vizag/RINL tag dispute)**
 - Customer insists the invoice says one mill (e.g., SAIL) but tag/MTC shows another (Vizag): "Vizag வந்துருக்கா 10 மட்டும் SAIL வந்துருக்கு." Resolution path used: get photo of tag, cross-check size/mill, re-issue corrected MTC with endorsement, courier originals after WhatsApp copy.
 - Lesson: always confirm **mill + size + grade match across tag, MTC, and invoice** before dispatch to avoid post-delivery compliance rejection at customer's site (especially govt/PSU sites requiring strict documentation).

3. **"Weight/size tolerance" objection from fabricators/transporters**
 - E.g., 2.5mm vs 2.6mm actual thickness causing weight overage that customer won't get paid for by their own end-client: "weight difference வந்து எங்களுக்கு காசு கொடுக்க மாட்டாங்க." Sales must flag tolerance issues upfront rather than let the buyer discover them at site.

4. **"Small quantity won't be served"**
 - New/small customers requesting small quantities told: "New customer-க்கு எல்லாம் சின்ன சின்ன quantity குடுக்குறது இல்ல sir." This is a stated minimum-order policy for unknown accounts — use judiciously, escalate to known/referred customers.

5. **Stock-outs on specific grade/mill**
 - "500 stop பண்ணிட்டாங்களா? ... R&L production இல்ல 3 months-ஆ" — reps should proactively explain supply-chain reasons (mill production pauses) rather than just saying "not available," and pivot to the available grade (550D) or alternate mill.

6. **Payment-timing / rate-lock disputes**
 - Classic pattern: customer wants today's rate locked but pays tomorrow; rep insists rate is valid only if payment/advance is received same day: "full payment இருந்தாதான் sir block பண்ண முடியும்." This must be stated clearly at quote time to avoid conflict later.

7. **Delivery/logistics delay pushback**
 - When cutting/coil prep delays dispatch, reps proactively buffer ("4-5 நாள் ஆகும்") and offer partial/interim lengths to keep the customer's site running — a good practice worth reinforcing in training.

## Effective Lines (openings, discovery, closing, follow-up)
**Openings** (brief, name + company, straight to business):
- "Hello Sir, Good Afternoon. [Name] பேசுறேன் Sir, இங்க [Company]-ல இருந்து."
- "Sir, group-ல நீங்க 20 mm sale CRS போட்டுருக்கீங்கல்ல? அது available-ஆ Sir?" — referencing a rate broadcast (group/WhatsApp) shows the business runs a rate-blast channel that reps follow up on individually — good practice to replicate.

**Discovery questions used effectively:**
- "என்ன grade/size/thickness வேணும்?" (grade, size, thickness) — always asked before quoting.
- "எவ்வளவு quantity வேணும்?" and "delivery location எங்க?" — quantity and location drive both price and transport cost; asked early and consistently.
- "என்ன brand தேவைப்படுது?" — brand preference clarified before quote (Sail vs Vaisakh vs local).

**Closing / urgency lines:**
- "Validity 2 days-ன்னு சொல்லிருக்காங்க" — creates urgency without being pushy.
- "order confirm பண்ணிடுங்க, நான் PO punch பண்றேன்" — pushing for immediate PO once rate is agreed.
- Offering a small concession to close rather than a price cut: "loading free பண்ணலாம், ஒன்னும் problem இல்ல."

**Follow-up discipline:**
- Reps repeatedly circle back same-day/next-day on pending enquiries: "இது எப்போ plan பண்றீங்க?" and proactively chase stuck quotations: "அந்த quotation best final-ஆ கொடுத்தீங்கன்னா..."
